objective: Sell and deliver two bounded USD 500 AI Clip Assembly pilots using existing customer-controlled footage and project-owned video proof, without promising new generation, native editor files, performance results, or unlimited revisions.

source_need.published_scope: Combine six existing AI-generated clips totalling about 32 seconds into one 30-45 second cinematic brand film and one 25-30 second website cut, with colour, music, sound, selected shot repair, high-resolution exports, and editable project files.
source_need.latest_status: The public listing remained available with the same USD 500 fixed price on 2026-09-08.
source_need.client_record_when_checked: United States; Upwork member since July 23, 2023; no client spend or hire history was visible on the public listing
source_need.demand_interpretation: A current buyer has attached a USD 500 budget to a bounded six-clip assembly problem. This validates the problem and price point, not LazyingArt demand or a likely award.

offer.scope: Up to six customer-controlled AI-generated clips and 45 seconds of combined source; one 30-45 second 16:9 master; one 25-30 second 16:9 web cut derived from the same edit; basic colour continuity; one music and sound pass; simple supplied titles or logo; H.264 MP4 exports; a source manifest; and one consolidated correction pass.
exclusions: Native Premiere Pro, After Effects, Final Cut, or DaVinci Resolve project delivery unless the accepted scope names and confirms the format
offer.qualification: Begin with a brief, source metadata, rights status, and private previews. Agree the story sentence, usable clips, native-project requirement, delivery, source handling, correction, cancellation, refund, and payment terms before original source transfer or payment.

examples: Six-source Madeira assembly with a 41.958-second master and a 27.816-second web cut
proof.quality_gate: A clip must pass a current human visual-quality review before it is featured as selling proof. Project ownership, a complete workflow, and technical delivery are necessary but not sufficient.

assembly_sample.technical_qa: Both live files load as 1280x720 H.264 with stereo AAC audio; neither local output contained a detected black interval of at least 0.5 seconds or silence of at least 0.8 seconds at -45 dB.
assembly_sample.claim_boundary: This is project-owned AI-assisted footage and editing-process evidence, not customer work, an advertising result, or proof that unseen buyer clips will fit.

proof.claim_boundary: Every public example is first-party project work. None is a customer brand film, paid UGC campaign, e-commerce performance result, or proof that six unseen source clips will fit.

linkedin.content:
Six AI-generated clips can still feel like six separate shots. The first edit decision isn't the transition. It's what should change between the first frame and the last.

I tried the exact constraint on six scenes from one of our own projects. About 43 seconds of source became one 42-second journey, then a 28-second web cut from the same timeline.

Both videos are here, with the source order, trims, export notes, and hashes:
https://lazying.art/video/brand-film/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ai_clip_assembly&utm_content=six_source_proof#sample

This is also the boundary for my fixed USD 500 assembly pilot: existing footage only, one master, one shorter cut, and one correction pass.
linkedin.pause_reason: Moved back to draft before release while the featured AI-generated media receives a fresh human quality review. Technical completion and provenance are not enough for active selling proof.
linkedin.policy: The item must stay in DRAFT until a human reviews the complete linked sample for story, motion, continuity, composition, audio, captions, and overall finish. A draft is not publication, a lead, or a sale.

funnel.gross_target_math: Two confirmed USD 500 payments equal USD 1,000 gross before fees, tax, refunds, and delivery costs.
